title: The Python Tutorial
description: The official introduction to the Python language and standard library, covering syntax, data structures, functions, modules, errors and classes in a readable sequence.
why_useful: The canonical source, kept current with the language itself. Starting here avoids the tutorials that teach Python 2 idioms or skip the standard library entirely.
learning_outcomes: Write and run Python scripts and modules confidently
Use lists, dicts, sets and comprehensions idiomatically
Understand imports, packages and virtual environments

title: NumPy: the absolute basics for beginners
description: Official introduction to NumPy arrays: creation, indexing, slicing, broadcasting, reshaping and basic operations, with runnable examples throughout.
why_useful: Array thinking is the prerequisite nobody announces. Broadcasting and shape errors cause more early frustration in ML than any algorithm does, and this page addresses both directly.
learning_outcomes: Create, index and reshape arrays without loops
Predict the result shape of a broadcast operation
Read the shape errors that dominate early debugging

title: 10 minutes to pandas
description: Official whirlwind tour of pandas: Series and DataFrames, selection, missing data, grouping, reshaping, merging, time series and plotting.
quality_notes: Titled ten minutes, but treat it as an orientation to come back to rather than a single sitting.
why_useful: Most of the work on a real project is data wrangling, and this is the shortest path to being able to load, inspect, group and join data without fighting the API.
learning_outcomes: Load, inspect and select from a DataFrame
Group and aggregate to answer questions about data
Handle missing values deliberately rather than by accident

title: Essence of linear algebra
description: Visual video series building geometric intuition for vectors, linear transformations, matrix multiplication, determinants, change of basis and eigenvectors.
author: Grant Sanderson
quality_notes: Builds intuition rather than computational fluency. Pair it with exercises from a course if you need to be able to compute, not just picture.
why_useful: Turns matrix algebra from symbol manipulation into something you can picture, which is what makes later topics like embeddings and attention feel reasonable rather than arbitrary.
learning_outcomes: Interpret a matrix as a transformation of space
Explain what eigenvectors are geometrically
Reason about dot products and projections visually

title: Essence of calculus
description: Visual video series deriving derivatives, the chain rule, integrals and Taylor series from geometric first principles rather than from rules to memorise.
author: Grant Sanderson
why_useful: The chain rule is the whole of backpropagation. Understanding it visually here means gradient descent later reads as an obvious consequence rather than a new thing to learn.
learning_outcomes: Explain a derivative as a rate of change, not a formula
Apply the chain rule with understanding of why it composes
Connect gradients to the idea of steepest ascent

title: MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra
description: Full university course with video lectures, problem sets and exams, covering solving linear systems, vector spaces, orthogonality, determinants, eigenvalues and applications.
author: Gilbert Strang
quality_notes: A full course with assessment, not a quick primer. Substantial time commitment.
why_useful: The depth option for linear algebra, with problem sets that build the computational fluency intuition-first video series deliberately skip.
learning_outcomes: Solve and reason about systems of linear equations
Work with vector spaces, rank and orthogonality
Compute and interpret eigenvalues and eigenvectors

title: Seeing Theory
description: Interactive visual introduction to probability and statistics, covering basic probability, compound probability, distributions, inference, regression and Bayesian methods.
quality_notes: An intuition builder rather than a course; it will not make you fluent at calculation on its own.
why_useful: Sampling distributions and confidence intervals are far easier to grasp when you can move a slider and watch them respond, which is exactly what this does.
learning_outcomes: Explain what a sampling distribution is
Interpret a confidence interval correctly
Distinguish frequentist and Bayesian framings of the same question

title: MIT 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms
description: University course covering asymptotic complexity, sorting, hashing, search trees, graph algorithms, dynamic programming and their implementation in Python.
why_useful: Optional for getting started in ML, but the complexity intuition it builds is what stops a pipeline from quietly becoming unusable once the data outgrows memory.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the time and space complexity of an approach
Choose appropriate data structures for a problem
Recognise when a dynamic programming formulation applies
